text:
ConocoPhillips fell nearly 1% today and is down 7.8% over two weeks, weighed down by a widening gap between U.S. and global oil prices. U.S. crude is trading at $96.41 per barrel while international crude sits at $114.89—an 18-dollar spread that reflects supply concerns abroad and potential constraints at home. News that the Trump administration is considering a diesel export ban added pressure, since refiners (a key part of ConocoPhillips' business) would face margin squeezes if they can't sell refined products globally at full value.

The broader backdrop is geopolitical tension with Iran and uncertainty about U.S. energy policy. Energy stocks got caught between rising interest rates pinching valuations and the Iran conflict creating unpredictable crude supply dynamics—two headwinds that can work against large-cap oil producers even when crude prices themselves remain elevated.
